chunks: And from him, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ and Sindī ibn Muḥammad together, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Saʿīd ibn Yasār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A woman upon whom salat (prayer) becomes forbidden, then she becomes pure and performs wudu (ablution) without performing ghusl (ritual bath) — may her husband approach her before she performs ghusl? He said: No, not until she performs ghusl. So the proper way regarding these reports is that we carry them upon a degree of karāhah, not prohibition, and the earlier reports upon permissibility. What indicates that is what follows.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), which is suspended during menstruation
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislikedness, indicating reprehensibility rather than prohibition
key_terms.تَطْهُرُ: becomes pure, meaning the menstrual bleeding has ceased

ai.seo_question: Can a husband have intercourse with his wife after menstruation ends but before ghusl?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on a husband approaching his wife after her menstrual bleeding has ceased but before she has performed ghusl. Although the Imam عليه السلام says not to do so until she performs ghusl, the passage then states that such reports are to be understood as indicating karāhah rather than outright prohibition, while earlier reports indicate permissibility.
